talks.title: Spotlight on DC010 Beijing with Jun Li
talks.teaser: DEF CON Groups ambassador Jayson Street interviews Jun Li, founder of DC010 Beijing, discussing community growth and technical events in China.
talks.summary:
### Building Hacker Communities in China
At 00:00, Jason E. Street, Global Coordinator for DEF CON Groups, sits down with Jun Li, founder of DC010 Beijing, during a joint community gathering with DC86755 in Shenzhen. Street and Li discuss the mission of fostering grassroots hacker culture in China.

### Origins and Academic Partnerships of DC010
At 02:01, Jun Li recounts the founding of DC010 Beijing. He describes navigating formal institutional approvals to establish a welcoming physical space where university students, software engineers, and cybersecurity hobbyists could meet, collaborate, and share technical knowledge.

### Community Growth and Hands-On Technical Workshops
At 03:52, Li reflects on the group's first year of operations. He details how DC010 organized monthly technical meetups, CTF competitions, and interactive tutorials covering reverse engineering and hardware security, noting that attendance rapidly expanded beyond initial expectations.

### Countering Social Stigmas Surrounding Hackers
Concluding between 05:47 and 09:33, Li and Street discuss broader cultural perceptions. Li explains how DC010 actively works to dispel negative media stereotypes surrounding hackers, demonstrating to the broader public that hacker communities foster essential education, responsible research, and constructive technical curiosity.

talks.title: 3D Printing Techniques for Hackers
talks.teaser: Dr3t from DC719 Colorado Springs delivers a detailed technical presentation on 3D printing workflows, filament tuning, and custom hacker jewelry design.
talks.summary:
### Practical 3D Printing for Hackers and Makers
At 00:15, speaker Dana Class opens a practical workshop on additive manufacturing, demonstrating how hackers can leverage 3D printing for functional prototyping, custom physical tools, and field hardware.

### Transitioning from Decorative Models to Functional Engineering
At 02:02, Class urges makers to look beyond aesthetic trinkets and decorative models. He demonstrates designing precise, load-bearing mechanical components, custom field enclosures, and tailored electronic chassis designed to withstand physical abuse.

### Medical Applications and Custom Prosthetics
At 04:03, the presentation highlights humanitarian and medical applications. Drawing from personal experience supporting wounded military veterans, Class shares techniques for 3D modeling and printing low-cost custom prosthetic limbs and ergonomic body adaptations.

### Rapid Prototyping and Scale Additive Construction
At 06:00, Class explores larger-scale additive manufacturing trends, discussing automated construction printing, modular emergency shelters, and rapid on-site fabrication of replacement parts in austere environments.

### Reverse Engineering and Physical Security Tools
Concluding between 08:02 and 12:00, the speaker demonstrates tactical hardware design. He details CAD modeling workflows for digitizing physical keys, fabricating custom badge holders, printing ergonomic lockpick handles, and selecting suitable filaments (PLA, ABS, PETG, and TPU) based on thermal and mechanical stress requirements.
